 FAA issues ground stop for all flights due to ‘extraordinary circumstances’
 4:20
 • Source:
 CNN 
 FAA issues ground stop for all flights due to ‘extraordinary circumstances’ 
 4:20
 Ad Feedback 
 What's happening now
 • Ground stop: All flights in the United States are grounded until further notice, “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” the Federal Aviation Administration said. An FAA spokesperson said there is a communications problem impacting Air Route Traffic Control Centers, which handle flights going across the country.
 • What officials are saying: The Homeland Security secretary said the ground stop did not stem from a threat to the US , and preliminary reports indicate this was not a cyberattack , law enforcement sources told CNN. President Donald Trump has been briefed .
 • Rare instance: The last time there was a nationwide ground stop was in January 2023, when a pilot notification system went down. Prior to that, the last nationwide ground stop was issued after the September 11, 2001, attacks.
 Read more 
 Updates

 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:26 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 At JFK, queued passengers call loved ones as they await more information
 By Zachary Slater 
 Some passengers flying to Savannah, Georgia, waited on a tarmac at John F. Kennedy International Airport for 90 minutes before an update came.
 Following the long wait, the pilot finally announced that it was not immediately clear what would happen next.
 Frustrated passengers peppered tired flight attendants with questions, asking about how checked bags would be retrieved if the plane returns to the gate and how the ground stop could impact flights tomorrow.
 Row by row, passengers called friends and family to let them know they probably won’t make it to their destination tonight.

 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:25 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 “Safety is always our top priority,” says Airlines for America
 By Emma Tucker 
 Airlines for America, the major trade association representing US airlines, said it’s in close communication with the Department of Transportation and the FAA regarding the nationwide ground stop, adding: “Safety is always our top priority.”
 “We appreciate the patience of the traveling public and the dedication of frontline employees who are navigating this situation.”
 The association encouraged impacted travelers to be in touch with their carrier for “real-time updates.”
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:19 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Ground stop caused by "temporary telecommunications outage," FAA says
 By Dalia Faheid 
 An airplane prepares to land at Miami International Airport on Friday. 
 Marco Bello/Reuters 
 The Federal Aviation Administration said the nationwide ground stop today was caused by a “temporary telecommunications outage.”
 The statement comes about an hour after Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy announced the ground stop.
 The agency said “out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted.”
 All flights have been accounted for and international flights “will be handled on a case by case basis,” the FAA said.
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:20 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 American Airlines says flights expected to be disrupted for the rest of the day
 By Tori B. Powell 
 Airplanes are parked on the tarmac at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Arlington, Virginia, on Friday. 
 Jonathan Ernst/Reuters 
 American Airlines flights are expected to face disruptions for the rest of the day depending on how long the nationwide ground stop currently in effect will last, the company said in a statement.
 “It will be all hands-on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible when the FAA lifts this ground stop,” American Airlines said.
 Flights already in the air can still continue to their destinations, the company added.

 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:18 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 No time frame in place to resolve communications outage, Mullin says
 By Kevin Liptak 
 Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said officials have not yet discussed a time frame for resolving the FAA communications outage as the administration focuses on passenger safety.
 “We have not discussed any timeframe,” he told reporters at the White House.
 “It’s going to take some time,” he went on. “And so this isn’t going to just be resolved and turned around within the hour.”

 Some ‘people appear to be unaware’: CNN reports across US airports amid FAA nationwide ground stop

 Some ‘people appear to be unaware’: CNN reports across US airports amid FAA nationwide ground stop 
 2:59
 At Chicago O’Hare International Airport, the mood remains relaxed. There’s a feeling the customers don’t grasp the extent of this nationwide ground stop.
 ANA Airlines offered a meal voucher for the two-hour delay to a flight from O’Hare to Haneda Airport in Tokyo with an email saying “we’re sorry about the change to your travel plans.”
 Periodically, a gate agent will announce there’s a ground stop but provide no further context. It feels like a minor inconvenience. People are sitting down waiting on the delay to be done.
 There’s no lines with gate agents. The only line of folks I’m seeing is for a Lufthansa flight that had customers line up to board.

 Link Copied!
 FAA issues and Microsoft outage are not connected, Mullin says
 By Molly English 
 Passengers look at departures and arrivals boards at Logan International Airport in Boston on Friday. 
 Brian Snyder/Reuters 
 Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said that yesterday’s massive global Microsoft outage and the communications problem causing today’s national FAA ground stop are not connected.
 “I don’t see any reason to connect those two at all,” Mullin told reporters at the White House Friday afternoon. “Those are separate issues.”
 Yesterday’s outage, which began around noon ET on Thursday, affected millions globally and left workers unable to access Outlook email, Teams meeting tools and other staples of modern office life . AI companies said they were facing issues as well. Banks, governments, health services, railways and courts all reported disruptions across Microsoft products .
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:13 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Mullin and Duffy have briefed Trump on the ground stop
 By Kevin Liptak 
 Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said President Donald Trump had been briefed by officials on the FAA ground stop for all flights, and has spoken on the phone with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy.
 “He was on the phone earlier with the president and several of us. And they’re doing a phenomenal job in a crisis mode,” Mullin said.
 He said Trump “took a lead in this immediately” and provided assets and communication to ensure the situation was managed.
 Read more 
 Updated Nov 13, 2026, 5:11 PM ET 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:10 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Homeland Security secretary says ground stop did not stem from a threat to the US
 By Kevin Liptak 
 Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin speaks with members of the press on the White House grounds on Friday. 
 Pool 
 Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin says there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat is behind a communications outage that grounded all US flights.
 Still, he said he would not rule out any cause for the outage, including a cyberattack.
 “There is no indication that we’ve had, no reason to believe, that as of right now this was a threat to the United States,” Mullin told reporters at the White House, later repeating there was “no indication as of yet that this was a nefarious attack against us.”
 “This was a telecommunication outage,” he asserted.
 He said all flights were accounted for, and that flights in the air were being dealt with on a “case by case” basis.

 All flights in the United States are grounded until further notice “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” the Federal Aviation Administration said. 
 The cause of the ground stop is still unknown. See what Transportation Security Administration wait times are looking like so far:

 What it's like inside the terminal in Newark right now
 By Brian Stelter 
 Here at Terminal A inside Newark Liberty International Airport, hundreds of would-be passengers are walking up to security, still hoping their flights will take off this evening. And nearly half of the departures are listed as “on time.”
 But some people arriving at the airport are staring up at the departure board in disbelief. And a few are huddling before the security checkpoint, debating whether to go ahead.
 A pair of workers from Toronto sat down on the ground next to me with their bags and started looking for a hotel in New York City for the night. Their flight has already been canceled, they said, and their work trip is suddenly bleeding into the weekend.
 But for the most part, it’s still business as usual here, oddly enough.

 Published Nov 13, 2026, 5:09 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 What is a ground stop?
 By Nicki Brown 
 Airplanes are parked on the tarmac at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Arlington, Virginia, on Friday. 
 Jonathan Ernst/Reuters 
 A ground stop is an order issued by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) that requires aircraft to remain on the ground and bars them from taking off. Planes already in flight are allowed to remain in the air.
 Some ground stops only cover certain types of planes or facilities, though the one issued Friday affects all aircraft across the United States.
 The last nationwide ground stop took place after a key pilot safety system went down in January 2023 . A contractor working for the FAA unintentionally deleted files related to the Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) system , prompting the FAA to issue a ground stop for a couple of hours. Thousands of flights were canceled or delayed. The NOTAM system, known at the time in the United States as “Notice to Air Missions,” provides updated information to pilots about potential hazards along a flight path or at an airport.
 Prior to 2023, the last nationwide ground stop was issued after the September 11, 2001, attacks.
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 4:55 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 When air traffic control goes down it's called ATC Zero
 By Aaron Cooper 
 Airplanes prepare to land at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Arlington, Virginia, on Friday. 
 Jonathan Ernst/Reuters 
 Some parts of the national airspace went to “ATC Zero” on Friday, a term that means no air traffic control services can be provided.
 “Approach is ATC Zero, and Chicago Center is close to being ATC Zero as well for equipment,” a controller warned pilots approaching Chicago in audio captured by the site ATC.com . “We lost all of the frequencies and all of the automation for the handoff and strips and stuff.”
 Air traffic controllers use radio frequencies to communicate and paper strips – or the electronic upgraded versions of them – to keep track of planes.
 Flights can continue to fly in airspace without air traffic control operating under visual flight rules, but most planes are going to be rerouted, prevented from taking off or grounded.

 Published Nov 13, 2026, 4:40 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Preliminary reports indicate this is not a cyberattack, law enforcement sources say
 By Evan Perez , Hannah Rabinowitz and Josh Campbell 
 An employee provides instructions to travelers at Hartsfield International Airport in Atlanta on Friday. 
 CNN 
 Preliminary reports indicate this is not a cyberattack, according to two law enforcement officials.
 FBI personnel across the country are continuing to monitor the situation, according to another law enforcement source.
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 4:30 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Ground stop followed a communication issue, Duffy says
 By Pete Muntean 
 The FAA issued the ground stop “following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said in a social media post. “FAA technicians are investigating the issue.”
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 4:31 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Nationwide ground stops are rare
 By Aaron Cooper and Pete Muntean 
 Airplanes are seen on the tarmac at Logan Airport in Boston during a nationwide ground stop on Friday. 
 WBZ 
 The last time there was a nationwide ground stop was in January 2023, when a pilot notification system went down.
 Prior to that, the last nationwide ground stop was issued after the September 11, 2001, attacks.
 Read more 
 Updated Nov 13, 2026, 4:28 PM ET 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 4:18 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 FAA issues nationwide ground stop for all flights
 By Pete Muntean and Aaron Cooper 
 All flights in the United States are grounded until further notice, “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” the Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement.
 The cause of the ground stop was not immediately clear, but an FAA spokesperson says there is a communications problem impacting Air Route Traffic Control Centers, which handle flights going across the country.
 “Traffic should remain ground stopped until further notice,” the FAA said in an advisory. “International flights will be managed on a case by case basis.”
